why: Reweighting C6 made the model more protective of determiner/head and required postmodifier boundaries while at the same time treating markers at NP tails or immediately before punctuation as milder; that moved the top-one/two cut preferences (rank_depth: depth1 down, depth2 up) so some long-latency top cuts improved but many medium-latency cuts (especially ≤7 and ≤5 bins) shifted into intra‑NP positions or split enumerations, producing roughly equal numbers better/worse and a small net drop.
lesson: Keep the stronger protection against splitting determiners/heads and required postmodifiers, but do not so aggressively lower severity for markers at NP tails / before punctuation that intra‑NP cuts and enumeration splits become more likely (test effects per latency bin, esp. ≤7).
